1. unattended-upgrades-install  [safe]  fixes UPD-001
   Install unattended-upgrades and turn it on with an apt.conf.d drop-in
   opt in: applied only when selected by id
   create   /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/90stackward-unattended-upgrades (0644)
            checked first with: apt-config dump -c <new file>
            --- /dev/null
            +++ b/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/90stackward-unattended-upgrades
            @@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
            +// Written by stackward: plan step unattended-upgrades, fixes UPD-001.
            +// Turns on the daily package list update and unattended-upgrades.
            +// Remove this file to undo.
            +APT::Periodic::Update-Package-Lists "1";
            +APT::Periodic::Unattended-Upgrade "1";
   run      env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=120 install -y unattended-upgrades
            # install unattended-upgrades (named here so nothing is installed silently)
   note     Installs the unattended-upgrades package (and what it depends on) from the configured apt sources with apt-get install. Nothing else is upgraded on purpose, but apt may upgrade a dependency the package needs. If the package lists are old, run apt update first, or the install fails and nothing else changes.
   note     Reboot decision: automatic reboot stays off, so updates that need a reboot (a kernel, libc) wait for you and SYS-002 reports them. To let unattended-upgrades reboot at 04:00 (host time) instead, apply the opt in step unattended-upgrades-reboot.
   note     Only the origins allowed in 50unattended-upgrades are installed; UPD-003 checks that the security pocket is among them.
   note     A file that sorts after 90stackward-unattended-upgrades in /etc/apt/apt.conf.d can still turn it off; the next audit's UPD-001 says so.
   undo     Remove the drop-in; unattended-upgrades then follows the distribution's own settings again. The package is purged; packages apt installed with it stay.
            rm -f /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/90stackward-unattended-upgrades
            env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=120 purge -y unattended-upgrades

2. unattended-upgrades-reboot  [networking]  fixes UPD-004
   Let unattended-upgrades reboot at 04:00 (host time) when an update needs it
   opt in: applied only when selected by id
   create   /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/91stackward-automatic-reboot (0644)
            checked first with: apt-config dump -c <new file>
            --- /dev/null
            +++ b/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/91stackward-automatic-reboot
            @@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
            +// Written by stackward: plan step unattended-upgrades-reboot.
            +// Lets unattended-upgrades reboot the host at 04:00 (host time)
            +// when an update needs a reboot. Remove this file to undo.
            +Unattended-Upgrade::Automatic-Reboot "true";
            +Unattended-Upgrade::Automatic-Reboot-Time "04:00";
   note     This is the reboot decision. stackward apply never reboots the host: this step only writes a setting. With it, unattended-upgrades reboots the host at 04:00 host time after a run that leaves /var/run/reboot-required. Without it, automatic reboot stays off and reboots wait for you.
   note     Logged in users do not hold the reboot back (Unattended-Upgrade::Automatic-Reboot-WithUsers is true unless set otherwise).
   note     unattended-upgrades is not installed: this setting takes effect once it is (the opt in step unattended-upgrades-install).
   undo     Remove the drop-in; automatic reboot is off again and reboots wait for you.
            rm -f /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/91stackward-automatic-reboot

3. fail2ban-sshd  [access-critical]  fixes CS-010
   Ban SSH brute force with a fail2ban sshd jail
   opt in: applied only when selected by id
   create   /etc/fail2ban/jail.d/90-stackward-sshd.local (0644)
            --- /dev/null
            +++ b/etc/fail2ban/jail.d/90-stackward-sshd.local
            @@ -0,0 +1,9 @@
            +# Written by stackward: plan step fail2ban-sshd, fixes CS-010.
            +# Bans SSH brute force on the sshd ports. Never bans loopback, the
            +# tailnet when Tailscale is in use, or the address the plan was made
            +# from. Remove this file and reload fail2ban to undo.
            +[sshd]
            +enabled = true
            +backend = systemd
            +port = 22
            +ignoreip = 127.0.0.1/8 ::1
   run      env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=120 install -y fail2ban
            # install fail2ban (named here so nothing is installed silently)
   run      fail2ban-client -t
            # check the whole fail2ban configuration with the new jail
   run      systemctl restart fail2ban
            # start fail2ban with the new jail
   restarts fail2ban
   note     Installs the fail2ban package (and what it depends on) from the configured apt sources with apt-get install. Nothing else is upgraded on purpose, but apt may upgrade a dependency it needs. If the package lists are old, run apt update first, or the install fails and the transaction rolls back.
   note     No SSH client address was known when this plan was made (a saved facts file, or not over SSH), so only loopback, the jail's own entries and the tailnet are ignored. apply refuses to run the step from an SSH session whose address the jail would not ignore: plan again from the session you will apply and confirm from.
   note     fail2ban-client -t checks the whole fail2ban configuration with the new file before fail2ban loads it; a failure stops the step and the transaction rolls back.
   note     The jail reads sshd's log from the systemd journal (backend = systemd), so it works on hosts without /var/log/auth.log; apt installs the python3-systemd module fail2ban recommends for it.
   undo     Remove the jail drop-in and purge fail2ban, which the step installed: its jails stop and every ban is lifted. Packages apt installed with it stay.
            rm -f /etc/fail2ban/jail.d/90-stackward-sshd.local
            env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=120 purge -y fail2ban
